data_source.global_landslide_inventory: NASA COOLR / UGLC Global Landslide Catalog

confidence_reason: Limited landslide inventory exists (ICIMOD, COOLR, UGLC) but coverage is sparse and uneven. Most remote areas have no documentation.
map_reliability_note: UNVALIDATED — Map is based on terrain proxies and sparse global inventory. Use for awareness and planning only. NOT for engineering design or siting.
warnings: Nepal has limited systematic landslide inventory. Most events in remote areas go unreported.
2015 Gorkha earthquake triggered thousands of landslides; many were documented but coverage is uneven.
SoilGrids 250m resolution is too coarse for steep Himalayan terrain. Local soil variability is extreme.
Global geology maps are extremely coarse for the Himalaya. Local geological complexity (thrust faults, metamorphic zones) is not captured.
Nepal has very high seismic hazard. Earthquake-triggered landslides are a major factor not fully captured in terrain-only models.
UNVALIDATED MAP: Sparse inventory coverage. Many landslide-prone areas have no documented events.
Himalayan terrain is extremely complex. A 30m DEM and 250m soil data miss critical local variations.
Monsoon rainfall triggers are highly localized. CHIRPS 5km data cannot capture orographic precipitation at slope scale.
recommendations: Contact Nepal Department of Mines and Geology for local geological maps.
Work with local communities to document landslide events (see Community Toolkit).
Contact ICIMOD for any existing landslide susceptibility studies in your district.
Use this map as a screening tool only. Site-specific geotechnical assessment is essential.
local_contacts: Department of Hydrology and Meteorology (DHM), Nepal — rainfall and some landslide data
ICIMOD — regional landslide research and inventory projects
NSET (National Society for Earthquake Technology) — community-based hazard data
